name: Antique Fuchsia
lede: Antique Fuchsia dulls fuchsia, the pink-purple flower named for the botanist Leonhard Fuchs, into a muted mauve-purple.

sections.title: A dulled flower color
sections.body:
The base word, fuchsia, names a flowering shrub itself named for the sixteenth-century German botanist Leonhard Fuchs; "antique" here means aged and dulled in tone, not literally old [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary is the earliest source for this exact shade in our library, and the ISCC-NBS system filed it in 1955 under block 223, a moderate purple [1][2]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[dull-purple]] and [[antique-fuchsia]], with [[razzmic-berry]] and [[dusky-mauve]] close by [3].

Fuchs himself never saw the color named for his flower: the plant was named for him by Charles Plumier decades after Fuchs's death, and the dye and paint industries only picked up the hue much later [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a rare tone in our archive: it covers at least one percent of the canvas in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors here [4]. One of the two is a 1905 Henri Matisse painting [4]. Both of our two matches come from the early twentieth century, too small a sample to say anything about which painters or periods favored this particular shade [4].
